ethylene is involved in insect defense in the maize genotype Mp708.
the ethylene signaling pathway mediates a maize resistance response to insect herbovory.
ethylene is required for the induction of the defense cysteine protease Mirl-CP and the resistance of maize plants to fall armyworm larvae.

the identification of the genes involved in the regulation of defense responses to insect herbivores in maize.
the identification of genes that are differentially expressed in the insect-resistant maize line Mp708 in response to herbivy.
the identification and characterization of the genes that control insect resistance in maize.

ethylene signaling mediates maize defense response to herbivore attack.
the ethylene signaling pathway mediates a maize plant's response to herbivorous insects.
ethylene is required for the induction of Mirl-CP in response to caterpillars feeding on Mp708.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the signaling pathways that enable Mp708 maize plants to mount defenses in response to fall armyworm feeding are complex, and that ethylene plays a role in this defense pathway.
